# Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere

Coordinate `EN-104-000-0007-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M3-C-AL-H-0634` | `PM-313.1` | status ACTIVE | original slug `Finite-generation-for-the-Kn-local-sphere-September-24-2026` | date 2026-09-24 | derived from the openai/math preprint Finite-generation-for-the-Kn-local-sphere-September-24-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove that the homotopy groups of the $`K(n)`$-local sphere are finitely generated ℤ<sub><i>p</i></sub>-modules in every integer degree, for every prime <i>p</i> and positive height <i>n</i>. Equivalently, the same conclusion holds after $`K(n)`$-localizing any finite <i>p</i>-local spectrum. This answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove that the homotopy groups of the $`K(n)`$-local sphere are finitely generated ℤ<sub><i>p</i></sub>-modules in every integer degree, for every prime <i>p</i> and positive height <i>n</i>. Equivalently, the same conclusion holds after $`K(n)`$-localizing any finite <i>p</i>-local spectrum. This answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland.

- **claim-integral-degreewise-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-descent-integral)): For every prime $p$, every integer $n\geq 1$, and every integer $t$, the $\mathbb Z_p$-module $$\pi_t L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$$ is finitely generated. Equivalently, for every finite $p$-local spectrum $F$, the module $\pi_t L_{K(n)}F$ is finitely generated over $\mathbb Z_p$ in every integer degree $t$.
  - Explanation: The local sphere has finitely generated integral homotopy in every degree. The equivalent formulation covers every finite local spectrum at the chosen prime.
- **claim-exact-bounded-step-cochains** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-cts-exact)): Consider an exact sequence of underlying vector spaces $$0\longrightarrow M'\xrightarrow{\iota}M\xrightarrow{q}M'' \longrightarrow0$$ whose maps and actions respect complete steps. Suppose that:* 1. *a bounded-step continuous map from a compact profinite space to $M$ with image in $\iota(M')$ is bounded-step continuous as a map to $M'$;* 2. *for every compact subset $T$ of a step of $M''$, there is a continuous map $s:T\to M_b$ into one step of $M$, with $qs=\mathop{\mathrm{id}}_T$.* *Then the corresponding sequence of continuous cochain complexes is short exact. In particular, it has the usual long exact cohomology sequence. These hypotheses hold for strict short exact sequences of compact $k$-spaces, for short exact sequences of finite modules over a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra with finite residue field, and for their localizations with the lattice steps just described.
  - Explanation: Detection of kernel continuity and continuous lifting of compact quotient images give exact continuous cochains and the resulting cohomology sequence.
- **claim-compact-envelope-resolution-comparison** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-cts-comparison)): Let $M$ satisfy <a href="#def:cts-steps" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:cts-steps">2</a>.* 1. *Every compact subset of a step of $M$ is contained in a compact $G$-stable $k$-subspace $N$ lying in one complete step. The action on $N$ is continuous. These $N$ form a filtered system whose union is $M$, and $$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M) =\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_N C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,N).$$* 2. *The ring $k[[G]]$ is Noetherian, and the trivial compact module $k$ has a resolution $P_\bullet$ by finitely generated free compact $k[[G]]$-modules. It may be unbounded. The comparison map $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{k[[G]],\mathrm{cts}}(P_\bullet,M) \simeq C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$$ is a natural quasi-isomorphism. Every term on the left is a finite power of $M$.* 3. *A right resolution by finitely generated free compact modules similarly defines $H_i(G,M)$. For compact $M$, cohomology and homology computed this way are compact Hausdorff, and continuous duality interchanges homology and cohomology, with the contragredient action on $M^\vee=\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{cts}}(M,k)$.* *For $G=\mathbb Z_p$ with generator $\gamma$, the cochain complex is $[M\xrightarrow{\gamma-1}M]$ in degrees $0,1$.
  - Explanation: Compact stable envelopes reduce bounded-step cochains to compact coefficients. Finite free completed resolutions compute the same cohomology and provide compact duality.
- **claim-equivariant-clopen-sections** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-cts-local-section)): Let $K$ be a normal uniform open subgroup of $G$, and let $X$ be a profinite $G$-space on which $K$ acts freely. Suppose that $X\to Y=K\backslash X$ has a continuous $K$-equivariant trivialization as a principal $K$-space. Put $H=G/K$. If $x\in X$ and $y$ is its image, the finite group $G_x$ maps isomorphically to $H_y$. There is an $H_y$-invariant clopen neighborhood $V$ of $y$ and a section $s:V\to X$, with $s(y)=x$, which is equivariant for $G_x\simeq H_y$.
  - Explanation: A local correction of a section makes it equivariant for the finite stabilizer while preserving its value at the specified point.
- **claim-uniform-finite-isotropy-vanishing** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-cts-isotropy-bound)): Fix a normal uniform open subgroup $K\subset G$, and put $d_G=\dim G$ and $a_G=[G:K]$. If $M$ is trace-admissible, then $$H^j(G,M)=0\qquad(j>a_Gd_G).$$ The same bound holds for $M\otimes_kV$ for every finite-dimensional continuous $G$-representation $V$. Neither the bound nor the choice of $K$ depends on $M$ or $V$.
  - Explanation: Trace elements give a uniform cohomological vanishing bound that persists under finite representation twists.
- **claim-full-stabilizer-duality** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-cts-full-duality)): Assume that the orientation character of $G$ is trivial over $k$. For every trace-admissible $M$ there are natural isomorphisms $$H_i(G,M)\simeq H^{d_G-i}(G,M) \qquad(i\in\mathbb Z).$$ Here homology is zero in negative degrees, and cohomology is zero in negative degrees. In particular $H^j(G,M)=0$ for $j>d_G$. The ordinary stabilizer $P_n$ has trivial orientation character and $d_G=n^2$, so this assertion applies to it without a twist.
  - Explanation: Trace admissibility and trivial orientation identify group homology with complementary-degree cohomology. The ordinary stabilizer has the required orientation.
- **claim-powered-division-freeness** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-mark-powered-division)): The algebra $D_m(\ell,b)$ is finite free of rank $p^{n\ell-b}$ over $A_m$. Its construction and action are intrinsic to relative Frobenius and commute with restriction to a deeper height locus. Every member of $\mathscr C_m$ is finite free over $A_m$, and reduction modulo $x$ sends $\mathscr C_m$ into $\mathscr C_{m+1}$.
  - Explanation: Monic division supplies a finite free powered division algebra. Relative Frobenius preserves the construction under specialization to the next height.
- **claim-integral-connected-jets** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-mark-jets)): For each $h\geq0$, the connected marking through exponent $p^h$ has a finite free model $H_{m,h}$ over $A_m$. There are coordinates $a_0,\ldots,a_h$ and polynomials in earlier coordinates such that $$\begin{aligned} a_0^{p^m-1}&=x,\\ a_i^{p^m}-x^{p^i}a_i&=P_i(a_0,\ldots,a_{i-1}), &&1\leq i\leq h. \end{aligned} \label{eq:mark-jet-equations}$$ If the first Hasse coefficient is normalized only up to a unit, the corresponding unit factors are inserted in these equations. The residue monomials $$a_0^{e_0}a_1^{e_1}\cdots a_h^{e_h},\qquad 0\leq e_0<p^m-1,\quad 0\leq e_i<p^m\ (i>0),$$ are an $A_m$-basis. The $G$-action preserves this model and admits a finite filtration with quotients integer powers of $\mathcal L_m$. The filtration remains such a filtration on every deeper height locus.
  - Explanation: Triangular monic equations construct the connected marking model. Its monomial filtration has periodicity-line quotients and survives specialization.
- **claim-whole-finite-marking-model** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-mark-whole-model)): For each such $U$ there are a finite free $A_m$-algebra $A'$, with integral multiplication laws in a fixed basis, and a $G$-invariant idempotent $e\in B'=A'[1/x]$ such that $$B_U=eB',\qquad B'/B_m\text{ is finite \'{e}tale}.$$ As a semilinear $A_m$-module, $A'$ has a finite filtration whose quotients are basic coefficients in $\mathscr C_m$. Its reduction modulo $x$ has such a filtration in $\mathscr C_{m+1}$. In a whole basis $A'=\bigoplus_\nu A_m b_\nu$, the $G$-action is given by continuous matrices over $A_m$. The base action is a continuous formal action preserving $(x)$; in particular the whole-basis action has a uniform pole bound, including for compact families of group elements.
  - Explanation: A whole finite free algebra carries the marking cover as a localized idempotent summand. Its integral basis controls boundary filtrations and the group action.
- **claim-generator-lift-root-algebras** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-mark-roots)): At level $\ell$, the reduced closure over $A_m$ of lifted geometric étale bases has coordinate algebra $$R_{m,\ell}=k[[t_{1,\ell},\ldots,t_{r,\ell}]].$$ If $s_i=t_{i,\ell}^{p^{m\ell}}$, the intermediate algebra generated by the $s_i$ over $A_m$ is $$S_{m,\ell}=k[[s_1,\ldots,s_r]],\qquad A_m\subseteq S_{m,\ell}.$$ After inverting $x$, $S_{m,\ell}[1/x]$ is the étale basis algebra, and $R_{m,\ell}[1/x]$ is its full generator-lift algebra. In particular the latter is the root extension of order $p^{m\ell}$, finite free of rank $p^{m\ell r}$, with no reduction of the lift scheme omitted. These identifications are natural under the $G$ action, changes of markings, and finite étale base change. For $j\leq\ell$, earlier division coordinates are integral series in the $p^{m(\ell-j)}$ powers of the level-$\ell$ coordinates. In particular the base parameters, in first-level coordinates, have order at least $p^m$.
  - Explanation: The lifted basis closure is a power-series algebra. Powered coordinates identify its localized full lift scheme with a finite free root extension, retaining its scheme structure.
- **claim-associated-basic-translation-representations** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-mark-associated-coefficients)): At full markings, each basic coefficient in <a href="#eq:mark-basic-coefficients" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:mark-basic-coefficients">[eq:mark-basic-coefficients]</a> is associated to a finite-dimensional translation representation over $k$. Its torsor, representation, and maps descend to finite marking levels, with the natural change-of-marking actions. A fixed finite collection of such data admits a common sufficiently deep level. The periodicity line already trivializes at the linear connected jet.
  - Explanation: Full markings identify basic coefficient bundles with finite translation representations. A finite collection of representations and maps descends together.
- **claim-geometric-trace-admissibility** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-mark-finite-isotropy)): Suppose $U$ is a torsion-free product marking subgroup as above. Every finite subgroup $F\subset G$ acts geometrically freely on $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}B_U$. There is an element $a_F\in B_U$ with $$\sum_{f\in F}f(a_F)=1.$$ Multiplication by $a_F$ is continuous between bounded-denominator steps of finite coefficient bundles. It also acts continuously on bounded analytic section and compact-support models, with compact profinite parameters retained. Thus the geometric coefficient modules satisfy the trace and module-action hypotheses of [prop:cts-isotropy-bound,prop:cts-full-duality]. Equivalently they satisfy <a href="#def:cts-trace" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:cts-trace">5</a>.
  - Explanation: Torsion-free marking subgroups force geometric freeness for finite stabilizer subgroups. This gives trace-one elements with the continuity needed for the geometric coefficient models.
- **claim-next-height-boundary-comparison** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-mark-strips)): Assume that $H^i_\mathrm{cts}(G,M)$ is finite for every $M\in\mathscr C_{m+1}$ and every $i\geq0$. Let $L$ be either a member of $\mathscr C_m$ or $A'\otimes_{A_m}M$ for $M\in\mathscr C_m$, where $A'$ is a whole model from <a href="#prop:mark-whole-model" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:mark-whole-model">13</a>. For any integers $a<b$, $$H^i_\mathrm{cts}(G,x^aL/x^bL)$$ is finite in every degree. For each fixed integer $a$, localization induces a map $$H^i_\mathrm{cts}(G,x^aL)\longrightarrow H^i_\mathrm{cts}(G,L[1/x])$$ with countable kernel and cokernel. These assertions concern whole lattices; they do not require a model for the idempotent $e$ on the closed locus.
  - Explanation: Finite boundary-strip cohomology follows from the next-height hypothesis. Its countable filtered union controls the kernel and cokernel of localization on whole lattices.
- **claim-covariant-honda-action** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-tower-honda-action)): The Honda universal-cover sheaf identifies covariantly with $\mathcal H_j$. This identification intertwines the original rational Honda endomorphisms with the bundle endomorphisms, preserving composition. Over a geometric base, it identifies $$D_j:=\mathop{\mathrm{End}}(\mathcal V_j)\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{End}}^0(\Gamma_j), \qquad P_j=\mathcal O_{D_j}^{\times}.$$ The invariant $1/j$ uses the arithmetic-Frobenius convention in the Honda presentation. The comparison is relative on perfectoid test bases and is linear over the sheaf $\underline{\mathbb Q_p}$ of continuous $\mathbb Q_p$-valued functions.
  - Explanation: The universal-cover comparison preserves composition of Honda endomorphisms and identifies the original integral automorphisms with the bundle-frame group.
- **claim-completed-tower-quotient** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-tower-comparison)): There is a choice of a fixed determinant-height normalization for which $$\label{eq:tower-quotient} [Z_\infty/G]\simeq(\mathcal N_m^r)_{\mathrm{ind}}.$$ The map $Z_\infty\to(\mathcal N_m^r)_{\mathrm{ind}}$ is a $G=P_n$-torsor. The comparison commutes with base change and with both integral marking actions of $J=P_m\times\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb Z_p)$. Under the convention that a matrix acts on a kernel framing by pushout, $(a,b)\in P_m\times\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb Z_p)$ acts on extensions by pullback along $a^{-1}$ on $\mathcal V_m$ and pushout along $b$ on $\mathcal O^r$.
  - Explanation: A fixed determinant normalization identifies the full marking quotient with independent extension tuples, retaining relative base change and both integral marking actions.
- **claim-analytic-etale-marking-tower** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-tower-etale-comparison)): Let $Z_\infty^{\mathrm{et}}$ denote the completed perfected tower of ordered étale Tate-module markings over $X_m$. There is a relative analytic isomorphism $$Z_\infty^{\mathrm{et}}\simeq(\mathcal H_n^r)_{\mathrm{ind}},$$ where independence is fiberwise over $\mathbb Q_p$. The isomorphism is equivariant for $G$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb Z_p)$. It is the restriction of an analytic isomorphism from the completed perfected tower of reduced closures $R_{m,l}$ to the open ball underlying $\mathcal H_n^r$.
  - Explanation: Normalized division limits identify the completed perfected étale marking tower with independent universal-cover sections, equivariantly and relatively.
- **claim-compact-torsor-support-descent** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-tower-supports)): The two compact torsors $$Z_U\ \longleftarrow\ Z_\infty \longrightarrow\ (\mathcal N_m^r)_{\mathrm{ind}}, \qquad\text{with groups }U\text{ and }G,$$ transport the preceding systems of support bounds cofinally. For the characteristic-$p$ function sheaf, and also with uniform compact profinite parameters, descent identifies $$\label{eq:tower-support-descent} \mathbf R\Gamma\bigl(G,\mathbf R\Gamma_c(Z_U,\mathcal O^\flat)\bigr) \simeq \mathbf R\Gamma\bigl(U,\mathbf R\Gamma_c( (\mathcal N_m^r)_{\mathrm{ind}},\mathcal O^\flat)\bigr).$$ The group cochain terms retain the support convention uniformly in their compact bar parameters.
  - Explanation: Compact torsors transport cofinal support bounds and identify the two equivariant compact-support complexes with uniform bar parameters.
- **claim-dense-banach-inverse-limits** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-kum-banach-limits)): Let $(E_j,f_j)$ be a countable inverse system of complete nonarchimedean normed vector spaces, with continuous linear maps $f_j:E_{j+1}\to E_j$ having dense image. Then $R^1\!\varprojlim_j E_j=0$. The assertion holds after replacing $E_j$ by $C(\mathcal D,E_j)$ with its supremum norm for any compact profinite $\mathcal D$. Consequently a countable inverse system of complexes having this property in each degree is computed by its termwise inverse limit.
  - Explanation: Density and completeness solve the countable difference equations defining the derived limit. The argument remains valid for uniform continuous parameter families.
- **claim-uniform-annular-narrowing** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-kum-annulus)): The Kummer tower on $A_S[a,b]$ gives a natural complex $$\label{eq:kum-difference} \mathbf R\Gamma(A_S[a,b],\mathcal O^\flat) \simeq \left[M_R[a,b]\xrightarrow{\gamma-1}M_R[a,b]\right], \qquad \gamma(T^u)=\epsilon^uT^u,$$ in degrees $0,1$. If $$\label{eq:kum-gap} a<a'<b'<b,\qquad a'/a\geq e^\kappa,\qquad b/b'\geq e^\kappa,$$ restriction to $A_S[a',b']$ is chain homotopic to its constant-monomial part. It therefore factors through $R[0]\oplus R[-1]$ in the derived category. The homotopy is bounded, linear over $R$, uniform for every compact profinite parameter, and compatible with base change and a translation of the coordinate by a relative section.
  - Explanation: A change of annular radii absorbs the nonconstant Kummer denominators and yields a bounded homotopy to the constant-monomial part.
- **claim-relative-line-disc-supports** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-kum-line)): The following statements hold over $S$, naturally under base change, with arbitrary retained compact profinite parameters.* 1. *There is a constant $A_p>1$, depending only on $p$ and the chosen Kummer generator, such that for $r_{\mathrm{out}}/r\geq A_p$ the map $$\mathbf R\Gamma(D_S(c,r_{\mathrm{out}}),\mathcal O^\flat) \longrightarrow\mathbf R\Gamma(D_S(c,r),\mathcal O^\flat)$$ factors through evaluation $R[0]$ followed by the constant inclusion. In particular, $$H^0(D_S(c,r),\mathcal O^\flat)=R,$$ and $$\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_{r\to0}\mathbf R\Gamma(D_S(c,r),\mathcal O^\flat)\simeq R[0].$$* 2. *Ordinary and compactly supported cohomology of the line are $$\label{eq:kum-line-values} \mathbf R\Gamma(\mathbb A_S,\mathcal O^\flat)\simeq R[0], \qquad \mathbf R\Gamma_c(\mathbb A_S,\mathcal O^\flat)\simeq R[-2].$$ For two concentric support discs with a sufficiently large radius ratio, the map from the smaller support complex to the larger one has pure degree-two image, carried isomorphically into the final compact-support cohomology. More precisely, if $A_r$ is the support complex for the disc of radius $r$ and $q_r:A_r\to R[-2]$ is extension of support to the whole line, the cone of $q_r$ maps cohomologically to zero after that fixed enlargement. The required ratio is uniform, also under bounded translations of the centers.* 3. *For $d$ ordered affine coordinates, the ordinary and section-germ complexes are $R[0]$, and the compact-support complex computed by cofinal boxes is $R[-2d]$. Maps between box-support bounds have pure degree-$2d$ image after a fixed enlargement in each coordinate.* 4. *The analogous relative assertions with $\mathbb F_p$ coefficients hold with the base complex $\mathbf R\Gamma(S,\mathbb F_p)$ in place of $R$. For $S=\mathop{\mathrm{Spa}}(C^\flat,\mathcal O_{C^\flat})\times\mathcal D$ this base complex is $C(\mathcal D,\mathbb F_p)[0]$. With the chosen geometric orientations, extension of constants identifies these line, section-germ, and support computations with the corresponding $R_{\mathcal D}$ computations above.* *The degree-two support class is unchanged by a translation of its section. Under inclusion of finitely many disjoint support discs into one larger disc, their degree-two classes add.
  - Explanation: Uniform annular homotopies give disc evaluation, ordinary affine-line sections, and oriented compact-support classes. Products retain ordered coordinates and compact parameters.
- **claim-low-degree-closed-graph-supports** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-kum-low-support)): Let $X$ be a bounded relative chart in an untilted affine space over a base v-sheaf $B$, with a slightly larger chart available for collars, and let $Z\subset X$ be closed. Assume the following conditions on this fixed bound.* 1. *After a finite cover of a slightly enlarged base bound by qc charts, $Z$ has a cofinal decreasing sequence of neighborhoods $T_j$, each a finite disjoint union of relative discs, or of boxes in at least one normal affine coordinate. Their centers are actual analytic sections on those charts.* 2. *On each chart, the clusters of $T_{j+1}$ refine those of $T_j$, and a fixed further refinement $j\mapsto j+N$ puts every child cluster in its parent with the radius ratio required in <a href="#prop:kum-line" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:kum-line">25</a>. The same $N$ works for every $j$, for all compact parameters, and on the finitely many support shells used for excision.* 3. *The cluster bounds have separated outer collars inside the enlarged output chart. Their intersection is $Z$, and their complements admissibly exhaust $X\setminus Z$.* *For $\mathscr F=\mathcal O^\flat$ or $\mathbb F_p$, put $$E_j=\operatorname{fib}\bigl(\mathbf R\Gamma(X,\mathscr F) \longrightarrow\mathbf R\Gamma(X\setminus T_j,\mathscr F) \bigr).$$ The inverse systems $H^0(E_j)$ and $H^1(E_j)$ are pro-zero. The same assertion holds relatively on the base and with compact parameters. Consequently the complex with support in $Z$ has no cohomology in degrees zero or one, and deletion of $Z$ preserves relative degree-zero sections. These conclusions hold also after a bounded-below descent calculation for which the finite chart refinements above can be made in each fixed total degree.* *For a closed locus $Z\subset Y$ in a possibly unbounded relative untilted affine space, the same low-degree support vanishing and degree-zero deletion statement hold if $Y$ has a compatible countable admissible exhaustion by interleaved bounds $X_a$ on which these hypotheses hold for $Z\cap X_a$. The tube systems and their required refinements may depend on $a$.
  - Explanation: Uniform child-to-parent support maps kill the low-degree inverse systems. Derived inverse limits then give low-degree closed-support vanishing and preserve ordinary sections under deletion.
- **claim-lattice-restriction-corestriction** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-ind-lattice-transitions)): Let $L$ be a lattice of rank $e$ in a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q_p$-vector space, and let $L'=p^{-1}L$. With trivial characteristic-$p$ coefficients, continuous cohomology is the exterior algebra on $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{cts}}(L,\mathbb F_p)$. Under the identifications from a lattice basis,* 1. *restriction from $L'$ to $L$ is zero in positive degrees and is the identity in degree zero;* 2. *corestriction from $L$ to $L'$ is zero in degrees less than $e$ and identifies the top-degree orientation lines.* *The assertions hold with coefficients $R_{\mathcal D}$ and with relative base complexes in place of $\mathbb F_p$.
  - Explanation: Lattice dilation kills positive restriction degrees and preserves only the top orientation under corestriction with characteristic coefficients.
- **claim-whole-extension-space-supports** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-ind-whole)): For every $s\geq 0$ there are natural comparisons $$\begin{aligned} \mathbf R\Gamma_c(\mathcal N_m^s\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathbb F_p) &\simeq E_{\mathcal D}[-(m+2)s], \label{eq:ind-whole-fp}\\ \mathbf R\Gamma_c(\mathcal N_m^s\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathcal O^\flat) &\simeq R_{\mathcal D}[-(m+2)s]. \label{eq:ind-whole-flat} \end{aligned}$$ A geometric Kummer orientation is understood. The comparison from the first formula to the second is extension of constants. It is compatible with continuous compact families of automorphisms and with all the support and lattice maps used below.
  - Explanation: Translation descent turns expanding supports into lattice corestrictions. The surviving lattice orientation combines with the affine support class.
- **claim-persistent-graph-tubes** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-ind-tubes)): Let a quasicompact perfectoid chart over $C^\flat$ carry untilted coordinates $z_1,\ldots,z_t$ whose classes in $\mathcal N_m$ are independent. Restrict to a bounded part of this chart and to a compact open slope patch in $\mathbb Q_p^t$. After a finite refinement of the base by quasicompact charts, the following constructions are available on each member of the refinement.* 1. *There are radii $0<\alpha<\beta$ and a fixed lattice $L\subset \mathbb Q_p^t\oplus F_m$ such that, on every geometric fiber, $$\label{eq:ind-persistent-lattice} L=\{w:\|\ell_z(w)\|\leq\alpha\} =\{w:\|\ell_z(w)\|<\beta\}, \qquad \ell_z(a,b)=\sum_i a_i z_i+b.$$ The same base chart has lattice $p^jL$ for the radii $\alpha\|p\|^j$ and $\beta\|p\|^j$, for every integer $j$.* 2. *Write $L_a=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathbb Q_p^t}(L)$ and $L_b=L\cap F_m$. At every sufficiently large $j$, the slope patch is a finite union of $p^jL_a$-cosets. Its graph in $\mathcal N_m$ has disjoint tubular neighborhoods indexed by those cosets. Each tube is the image of an actual relative disc, centered at a section $\sum_i a_i z_i$ for a constant representative $a$, modulo the compact translation lattice $p^jL_b$.* 3. *The closed tubes of radius $\alpha\|p\|^j$ and the open tubes of radius $\beta\|p\|^j$ are interleaved and cofinal among neighborhoods of the graph family. The construction works on a slightly enlarged independent-base bound and on its support collars, and it retains an arbitrary compact profinite parameter $\mathcal D$.* *For finitely many added coordinates and compact open patches of matrices of slopes, take products of these constructions. Their finite base refinements can be chosen simultaneously.
  - Explanation: Uniform norm equivalence on independent charts constructs persistent coefficient lattices and disjoint graph tubes at every depth.
- **claim-rank-germ-excision** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-ind-germ-excision)): There is a natural triangle $$\label{eq:ind-rank-triangle} \mathbf R\Gamma_c(X_{s,\geq t+1},\mathscr E) \longrightarrow \mathbf R\Gamma_c(X_{s,\geq t},\mathscr E) \longrightarrow \mathcal G_{s,t}(\mathscr E) \longrightarrow \mathbf R\Gamma_c(X_{s,\geq t+1},\mathscr E)[1],$$ where $\mathcal G_{s,t}$ is computed by shrinking neighborhood germs of $Z_{s,t}$, with compact support along that locus. Locally on a compact open Grassmannian graph patch $P$, it is $$\label{eq:ind-germ-formula} \operatorname{LC}\bigl(P, \mathbf R\Gamma_c(Y_t,\mathscr E)\bigr).$$ Here $\operatorname{LC}(P,-)$ means the filtered colimit of finite direct sums over finite clopen partitions of $P$. With an external compact parameter $\mathcal D$, the corresponding formula is $$\operatorname{LC}\bigl(P, \mathbf R\Gamma_c(Y_t\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathscr E)\bigr).$$ At each tube depth only a finite partition of $P$ is used, while $\mathcal D$ remains in the base complex. The slope-partition colimit is algebraic.
  - Explanation: Rank deletion produces a compact-support triangle whose third term uses shrinking neighborhood restrictions. Finite slope partitions give algebraic locally constant families.
- **claim-independent-tuples-scalar-comparison** (classification, [source](#stmt-thm-ind-comparison)): For every $s\geq0$ and every compact profinite $\mathcal D$, extension of constants induces natural quasi-isomorphisms $$\begin{aligned} E_{\mathcal D}\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}\mathbf R\Gamma_c(Y_s,\mathbb F_p) &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathbf R\Gamma_c(Y_s\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathbb F_p), \label{eq:ind-fp-parameters}\\ R_{\mathcal D}\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}\mathbf R\Gamma_c(Y_s,\mathbb F_p) &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathbf R\Gamma_c(Y_s\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathcal O^\flat). \label{eq:ind-algebraic-comparison} \end{aligned}$$ The tensors are algebraic. The comparisons retain uniform support and all compact bar parameters.* *Each $H_c^i(Y_s,\mathbb F_p)$ is a countable smooth admissible $M_s$-module. It has a smooth commuting $P_m$-action. Smooth means that each vector has open stabilizer; admissible means that every open subgroup of $M_s$ has finite-dimensional fixed space.
  - Explanation: Successive rank deletion proves algebraic scalar comparison and makes compact-support cohomology countable, smooth, and admissible for the integral matrix group.
- **claim-admissible-coefficient-group-cohomology** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-ind-admissible-cohomology)): Let $H$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group and let $V$ be a countable smooth admissible $\mathbb F_p[H]$-module. Then $H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V)$ is finite-dimensional for every $a$. Let $H$ act trivially on the external parameter $\mathcal D$ and on $R_{\mathcal D}$, and diagonally through $V$ on $R_{\mathcal D}\otimes V$. For the coefficient topology supplied by uniform finite-span families, there is a natural isomorphism $$H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,R_{\mathcal D}\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}V) \cong R_{\mathcal D}\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V).$$
  - Explanation: The compact dual of an admissible smooth module is finitely generated over the completed group algebra. Finite free resolutions give finite cohomology and compatible scalar extension.
- **claim-finite-equivariant-geometric-supports** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-ind-finite)): Let $1\leq m<n$, $r=n-m$, and let $U\subset P_m\times\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb Z_p)$ be a sufficiently deep product open subgroup as in <a href="#thm:tower-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:tower-comparison">19</a>. Let $Z_U$ be the perfected analytic cover associated with $B_U$ over $$0<\|x\|<1,\qquad \|y_i\|<1.$$ Then $$H^j\mathbf R\Gamma\bigl(G,\mathbf R\Gamma_c(Z_U,\mathcal O^\flat)\bigr)$$ is finite-dimensional over $C^\flat$ for every integer $j$. With an external compact profinite parameter $\mathcal D$, the corresponding groups are obtained by extension to $R_{\mathcal D}$ and are finite over that ring.
  - Explanation: Support descent and successive cohomology of the product marking groups yield finite-dimensional equivariant compact-support cohomology.
- **claim-independent-locus-ordinary-functions** (classification, [source](#stmt-cor-ind-functions)): For every $s\geq0$, $$\label{eq:ind-ordinary-functions} \Gamma(Y_s,\mathcal O^\flat)=C^\flat, \qquad \Gamma(Y_s\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathcal O^\flat) =R_{\mathcal D}.$$ The identifications are by pullback of scalars. For $s\geq1$, projection $Y_s\to Y_{s-1}$ has relative degree-zero direct image $\mathcal O^\flat$.* *Consequently a $G$-invariant algebraic function in a fixed finite marked coefficient model becomes a scalar after pullback to the completed full marking tower. If the model and its chosen component are defined over the finite field $k$, that scalar belongs to $k$. In particular this applies to invariant algebraic units.
  - Explanation: Closed-graph support vanishing identifies ordinary functions with base scalars. Invariant algebraic functions in a finite model consequently lie in its finite constant field.
- **claim-natural-root-diagrams** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-trans-roots)): Assume $m>1$. With the powers in <a href="#eq:trans-powers" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:trans-powers">[eq:trans-powers]</a>, there is a natural $G$-equivariant isomorphism $$V_{\mathop{\mathrm{Coind}}_q(E)}\simeq (V_E)^{1/h}. \label{eq:trans-root-functor}$$ It is compatible with the natural auxiliary actions and with every arrow of a finite diagram. It preserves exact diagrams and is compatible with successive coinduction and successive roots. For any fixed initial diagram, these assertions hold at every sufficiently deep finite marking stage, retaining the natural auxiliary action on each of its coinductions.
  - Explanation: The torsor power identity identifies coinduced finite diagrams with root diagrams. The comparison retains auxiliary marking actions and exactness.
- **claim-invariant-volume-cartier-functional** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-trans-volume)): After one finite marking shrink to a pro-$p$ subgroup, $\widehat\Omega^1_{R/k}$ has a $G$-invariant frame. In particular it has a $G$-invariant volume generator $\eta\in\widehat\Omega^r_{R/k}$.* *For a finite root order $h$ fixing $k$, the normalized Cartier functional $$T_{\eta,h}:R^{1/h}\longrightarrow R, \qquad T_{\eta,h}(z)=\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{C}}^{\log_p h}(z^h\eta)}{\eta} \label{eq:trans-cartier-functional}$$ is $R$-linear and generates $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_R(R^{1/h},R)$ as a module over $R^{1/h}$. A nonzero translation augmentation at the corresponding finite torsor level induces a scalar multiple of this functional; the scalar belongs to the chosen finite constant field.
  - Explanation: A finite marking shrink gives an invariant differential frame. Its volume normalizes a Cartier dual generator, and invariant ordinary functions make the torsor comparison scalar constant.
- **claim-fixed-transfer-pole-control** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-trans-cartier)): At the finite marking stage of , the operator $$S(f)=\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{C}}^{\nu_0}(f\eta)}{\eta}\quad(f\in R) \label{eq:trans-S}$$ is continuous, $k$-linear, and $G$-equivariant. It satisfies $S(b^{h_0}f)=bS(f)$. For $m>1$, the maps on $R$ induced by nonzero translation augmentations $\mathsf N_{q_0^a}\to k$, after the root identification, are nonzero scalar multiples of $S^a$. For $m=1$ one can choose the toral frame so that $$S\mathop{\mathrm{Fr}}^{\nu_0}=1. \label{eq:trans-height-one-split}$$* *Extend $S$ to $B'$ by $S(f)=S(ef)$, with image in $eB'$. There is a fixed integer $c\geq0$ such that, for every integer $D$, $$S(x^{-D}A')\subset x^{-\lceil D/h_0\rceil-c}A'. \label{eq:trans-pole-bound}$$ Every sufficiently large $D_0$ makes $\mathcal P=x^{-D_0}A'$ stable under $S$. Every fixed bounded-pole lattice, including any compact family of cochains with values in it, is carried into $\mathcal P$ by all sufficiently large iterates.* *The volume, its inverse, the whole trace-pairing matrices and their inverses have one fixed pole bound $c'$. In the normalized basis $b_i^{1/h}$, $h=h_0^a$, their transported matrices have pole losses at most $c'/h$. The normalized Cartier maps are adjoint to the inclusions of root Laurent representatives under the residue pairings with the transported volumes.
  - Explanation: A single normalized Cartier transfer realizes all iterated augmentation maps and contracts pole orders into a stable compact lattice.
- **claim-fixed-diagram-boundary-pole-loss** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-trans-diagram-bound)): Fix a finite Yoneda diagram of translation representations, descend it at a finite marking stage, and fix a cohomological degree. Its successive boundary maps can be represented by an operator on cocycles that loses at most one fixed $x$-pole order. Under , all of its coinduced diagrams use the roots of this same operator and its chosen splittings.
  - Explanation: Fixed sections of a finite Yoneda diagram bound the total boundary pole loss. Coinduction transports these same sections rather than introducing new estimates.
- **claim-laurent-support-model** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-laurent-model)): With the uniform compact-support convention of <a href="#lem:tower-supports" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:tower-supports">21</a>, there are natural quasi-isomorphisms $$\label{eq:laurent-descent} \mathbf R\Gamma_c(Z_U,\mathcal O^\flat;\mathcal D) \simeq\mathscr W_{\mathcal D}[-r], \qquad \mathbf R\Gamma_c(Z_U,\mathcal O^\flat;\mathcal D)^{\varphi=1} \simeq W_{\mathcal D}[-r].$$ They are compatible with finite marking maps, the idempotent $e$, and the actions defined over $k$. The support cohomology is therefore concentrated in cohomological degree $r$, both before and after coefficient descent. Every fixed normalized root basis $b_1^{1/h},\ldots,b_N^{1/h}$ gives the same module and the same complete-step category.
  - Explanation: Finite support diagrams reduce to a weighted Laurent module. Coefficient-only Frobenius descent gives its finite-field form without bounding root denominators.
- **claim-laurent-joint-continuity** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-laurent-action)): The $G$-action on $W$ and on $\mathscr W_{\mathcal D}$ is jointly continuous from a complete step, with a compact set of group and parameter values, into a complete step. It is uniformly equicontinuous there. The same holds for multiplication by the finite marked function algebra, fixed root-basis changes, and the finite matrices occurring in continuous group resolutions. Absolute Frobenius is an invertible additive operator on these modules. Its sufficiently divisible powers fixing $k$ commute with $G$ and act by chain automorphisms on the group complexes over $k$.
  - Explanation: Integral substitutions and finite basis matrices act continuously and equicontinuously between weighted complete steps. Absolute Frobenius gives invertible additive chain operations.
- **claim-finite-laurent-cohomology-homology** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-laurent-finite)): At every sufficiently deep product marking level used in <a href="#cor:ind-finite" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cor:ind-finite">35</a>, both $H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,W)$ and $H_i^{\mathrm{cts}}(G,W)$ are finite-dimensional over $k$ for every $a,i\geq0$. Since $k$ is finite, these are finite groups.
  - Explanation: Geometric support finiteness descends through coefficient Frobenius. Trace-admissible full-group duality then gives finite homology as well as cohomology.
- **claim-discrete-residue-quotient** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-cutoff-residue)): The finite-level pairings extend uniquely to an exact sequence of $k[G]$-modules $$0\longrightarrow W_+\longrightarrow W \xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }Q\longrightarrow0. \label{eq:cutoff-residue-sequence}$$ The map $\pi$ is continuous on every complete coefficient step into the discrete countable module $Q$, including on compact parameter families. It is equivariant for the actual group actions on the support and compact-dual models. All these assertions allow arbitrary root denominators in $W$.
  - Explanation: Finite residue tests extend by bounded-order truncation to arbitrary root denominators. Their kernel is precisely the positive Laurent subspace.
- **claim-positive-frobenius-contraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-cutoff-contraction)): For every integer $\nu\geq0$ and every tuple $w\in W_+^\nu$, there are an integer $a_*\geq0$, a complete weighted step written in the original whole basis, and $\epsilon,\alpha>0$ such that all $\Phi^{a_*+a}w$ belong to the closed subspace with x-order at least $\epsilon$, and $$\\|\Phi^{a_*+a}w\\|\leq \exp(-\alpha h_0^a)\quad(a\geq0). \label{eq:cutoff-contraction}$$ The statement applies without a bound on the root denominators of the coefficient series.
  - Explanation: Clearing the fixed basis denominator and enlarging a weight places all forward powers in one positive complete step with contracting norm.
- **claim-analytic-countable-index-openness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-cutoff-polish)): Let $Z$ be a Polish topological group and $B\subseteq Z$ an analytic subgroup in the sense of descriptive set theory: $B$ is a continuous image of a Polish space. If $Z/B$ is countable, then $B$ is open.
  - Explanation: The Baire property and the subgroup form of Pettis's theorem make an analytic subgroup of countable index open.
- **claim-positive-laurent-homology-vanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-cutoff-positive-acyclic)): For the completed-resolution group homology of <a href="#sec:continuous" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:continuous">2</a>, $$H_i(G,W_+)=0\qquad(i\geq0).$$
  - Explanation: Countability makes actual boundaries open in each complete positive cycle space. Frobenius contraction and its inverse turn every cycle into a boundary.
- **claim-finite-stable-compact-transfer-image** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-cutoff-stable)): For every $i\geq0$ the compact vector space $M_i=H^i(G,\mathcal P)$ satisfies $$I_i:=\bigcap_{a\geq0}S^aM_i\quad\text{is finite}. \label{eq:cutoff-stable}$$ No uniform bound on its size as the prime, height, degree, or finite marking level varies is asserted.
  - Explanation: Dualizing finite homology of the residue quotient gives a finite transfer inverse limit that surjects onto the compact stable image.
- **claim-compact-operator-module-structure** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-cutoff-compact-operator)): Let $M$ be a profinite $k$-vector space and let $S:M\to M$ be a continuous linear map. Assume that $I=\bigcap_{a\geq0}S^aM$ and $M/SM$ are finite. Then $S$ is an automorphism of $I$, and $V=M/I$ is a finitely generated $k[[z]]$-module with $z$ acting by $S$. Its original topology is the z-adic topology. The locally nilpotent subgroup $$T_S(M)=\bigcup_{a\geq0}\ker(S^a:M\to M)$$ is finite and closed. In particular $\ker S$ is finite.
  - Explanation: Removing a finite stable image leaves a contracting power-series module. Finite cokernel gives finite generation and finite locally nilpotent torsion.
- **claim-finite-localized-transfer-intersection** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-cutoff-compact)): Fix $i\geq0$ and $N\geq1$. Suppose $$S^NX_i/S^{N+1}X_i\quad\text{is countable}. \label{eq:cutoff-consecutive-hypothesis}$$ Then $S^NM_i/S^{N+1}M_i$ is finite, and $(S^NM_i)/I_i$ is a finitely generated $k[[z]]$-module with $z=S$. The operator $S$ on $S^NX_i$ has countable kernel and cokernel. Moreover $\ker(f_i\|_{S^NM_i})$ is finite and closed, $f_i$ is injective on $I_i$, and $$\bigcap_{a\geq0}\mathop{\mathrm{im}}(S^aM_i\longrightarrow X_i) =f_i(I_i)\cong I_i. \label{eq:cutoff-localized-intersection}$$ In particular the intersection is finite. No topology on $X_i$ and no closed-image assertion for its cochain differential is required.
  - Explanation: A countable consecutive quotient becomes finite on the compact side. Eventual integrality makes the localization kernel nilpotent and identifies the localized intersection with the finite stable image.
- **claim-fixed-marking-countability** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-pro-countability)): Assume the next-height coefficient-finiteness hypothesis of <a href="#lem:mark-strips" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:mark-strips">17</a>. There is an index $\nu_0$ such that $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,B_{U_\nu}) \quad\text{is countable-dimensional over $k$}$$ for every $\nu\geq\nu_0$ and every integer $i$.
  - Explanation: The next-height hypothesis yields countable open cohomology at every marking level on a common sufficiently deep tail.
- **claim-pro-constant-closure-stabilization** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-pro-constants)): For an abelian category $\mathcal B$, the constant objects in $\operatorname{Pro}(\mathcal B)$ are closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between them, and under extensions. If a decreasing system of subobjects $J_a\subset X$ represents a constant subobject $I\subset X$ in $\operatorname{Pro}(\mathcal B)$, then $J_a=I$ for all sufficiently large $a$.
  - Explanation: Constant pro-objects are closed under the stated exact constructions. A decreasing family representing a constant subobject eventually equals that subobject.
- **claim-uniform-transfer-image-stabilization** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-pro-stabilization)): For every $i$, the pro-object $\overline T^{\,i}(\Lambda)$ is constant, and its canonical projection to $T^i(k)$ is monic. It is annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. Moreover, there is an integer $N_i\geq1$, independent of the sufficiently deep marking level, such that $$S^{N_i}X^i_\nu/S^{N_i+1}X^i_\nu \quad\text{is countable-dimensional for all sufficiently large $\nu$}.$$
  - Explanation: Exact pro-completion and descending induction make the completed cohomology object constant and annihilated by the maximal ideal. Consecutive transfer images then agree modulo countable spaces uniformly on a marking tail.
- **claim-finite-yoneda-ext-comparison** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-pro-finite-ext)): For finite-length $\Lambda$-modules $E,F$, the natural map $$\operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal C}(E,F) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Ext}^j_\Lambda(E,F)$$ is an isomorphism for every $j$. Here the left side is Yoneda Ext: its classes are represented by exact diagrams whose middle terms all have finite length.
  - Explanation: Finite-length Yoneda extensions compute ordinary module Ext. Finite subdiagrams realize both extension classes and their comparisons.
- **claim-surjective-top-koszul-operation** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-pro-top-operation)): Suppose $T^\bullet(k)$ is not zero, and let $b$ be its largest nonzero degree. There is an allowed power index $s=q_0^{a_s}$ and a generator $$e_s\in\operatorname{Ext}^d_\Lambda(\mathsf N_s,k)$$ whose operation is an epimorphism in $\mathcal A$: $$e_s:T^{b-d}(\mathsf N_s)\longrightarrow T^b(k).$$
  - Explanation: Forward Koszul comparisons eliminate outgoing differentials from the top column and produce a finite Yoneda operation surjecting onto the highest nonzero cohomology object.
- **claim-common-equivariant-forgetting-shrink** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-pro-common-shrink)): Let $U$ be a uniform pro-$p$ marking subgroup, and let $E,F$ be finite objects of $\mathcal R_U$. Each group $\operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal R_U}(E,F)$ is finite. There is one open subgroup $U'\subset U$ on which every element of the kernel of $$\operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal R_U}(E,F) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^j_T(E,F)$$ becomes zero.
  - Explanation: Finite equivariant Ext makes its forgetting kernel a finite set. A common open subgroup kills all classes in that kernel.
- **claim-fixed-extension-all-high-transfers** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-pro-high-transfer)): Fix the index $s$ and generator $e_s$ of <a href="#prop:pro-top-operation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:pro-top-operation">57</a>, and choose a generator $e'_0\in\operatorname{Ext}^d_\Lambda(k,k)$. There is one sufficiently deep marking subgroup $U_*$ such that for every allowed $q\geq s$ the composite $$\label{eq:pro-composite-extension} \mathsf N_s\longrightarrow\mathsf N_q \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Coind}_q(e'_0)} \mathsf N_q[d]\longrightarrow k[d]$$ equals a nonzero scalar multiple of $e_s$ in the equivariant Ext group for $T\rtimes U_*$. The first and last maps use the natural auxiliary actions, which are retained for every $q$.
  - Explanation: The ordinary top Ext calculation is nonzero for every high coinduction. A common shrink kills all equivariant discrepancies at the fixed endpoints.
- **claim-allowed-coefficient-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-coeff-finite)): For every $1\leq m\leq n$, every coefficient module $M$ in over $A_m$, and every $i\geq0$, the group $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n,M)$$ is finite. In particular, this holds for every integer periodicity twist of $A_m$.
  - Explanation: Downward height induction combines fixed-level open countability with finite boundary strips. Compact Hausdorff coefficient cohomology is then finite.
- **claim-basic-representation-countability** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-coeff-finite-representations)): Assume the coefficient finiteness assertion at height $m+1$. For a basic coefficient $M$ over $A_m$, including any fixed tensor product of the basic division-tuple coefficients and an integer periodicity twist, there is a sufficiently deep normal product level $U$ such that $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}\bigl(G,B_U\otimes_{A_m}M\bigr)$$ is countable for every $i\geq0$. The same conclusion holds after further shrinking within the chosen cofinal sequence.
  - Explanation: Scalar countability extends to basic coefficients through finite translation filtrations or multiplicative-type regular summands, on a common finite marking tail.
- **claim-finite-marking-countability-descent** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-coeff-finite-descent)): Let $M_B$ be a finite locally free $B$-module with the coefficient action of $G$, and let $U\triangleleft J$ be a finite marking level. If $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,B_U\otimes_B M_B)$$ is countable for every $i\geq0$, then $H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M_B)$ is countable for every $i\geq0$. The order of $J/U$ need not be invertible in $k$.
  - Explanation: A bounded continuous contraction of the augmented torsor complex gives a descent spectral sequence preserving countability without division by the marking-group order.
- **claim-morava-modp-coefficient-finiteness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-coeff-morava)): Let $E_n$ be Morava $E$-theory for the height-$n$ Honda group over $\mathbb F_{p^n}$, and let $$\mathbb G_n=P_n\rtimes\mathop{\mathrm{Gal}}(\mathbb F_{p^n}/\mathbb F_p)$$ be its extended stabilizer. For every $i\geq0$ and every $t\in\mathbb Z$, both groups $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}\bigl(P_n,\pi_t(E_n/p)\bigr),\qquad H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}\bigl(\mathbb G_n,\pi_t(E_n/p)\bigr)$$ are finite.
  - Explanation: Periodicity twists give finite ordinary stabilizer cohomology. Finite Galois descent gives the same conclusion for the extended stabilizer.
- **claim-local-moore-degreewise-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-sphere-modp)): For every prime $p$, every $n\geq1$, and every $j\in\mathbb Z$, the group $$\pi_jL_{K(n)}(S/p)$$ is finite.
  - Explanation: Finite descent entries and a later horizontal vanishing line leave a finite filtration in each homotopy degree.
- **claim-derived-complete-finiteness-criterion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-sphere-completion)): Let $X$ be a derived $p$-complete spectrum. If $\pi_j(X/p)$ is finite for every $j\in\mathbb Z$, then $\pi_jX$ is finitely generated over $\mathbb Z_p$ for every $j\in\mathbb Z$. Conversely, finite generation of all $\pi_jX$ over $\mathbb Z_p$ implies finiteness of all $\pi_j(X/p)$.
  - Explanation: Finite power cofibers present integral homotopy as compact modules with finite residue quotient. Compact Nakayama gives finite generation, and the cofiber sequence proves the converse.
- **claim-local-sphere-free-ranks** (classification, [source](#stmt-cor-sphere-ranks)): For every prime $p$, every $n\geq1$, and every $j\in\mathbb Z$, the free rank is $$\label{eq:sphere-ranks} r_{p,n,j} =\#\left\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}: \sum_{i\in I}(1-2i)=j\right\}.$$ Equivalently, these ranks are the graded dimensions of the exterior $\mathbb Q_p$-algebra on generators in degrees $-1,-3,\ldots,-(2n-1)$.
  - Explanation: Finite generation converts the rational exterior-algebra calculation into exact free ranks, expressed by finite subset counts.
- **claim-odd-prime-height-one-groups** (classification, [source](#stmt-prop-sphere-height-one)): Let $p$ be odd. Then, for every $j\in\mathbb Z$, $$\pi_jL_{K(1)}S_p^\wedge\cong \begin{cases} \mathbb Z_p, & j=0\text{ or }j=-1,\\ \mathbb Z/p^{\,1+\nu_p(t)}, & j=2t-1,\quad0\neq t\in(p-1)\mathbb Z,\\ 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases}$$ The displayed groups include all additive extensions.
  - Explanation: The Adams-operation fiber computes every additive group at height one for odd primes, including the cyclic torsion and all additive extensions.

        "exact_quote": "Consider an exact sequence of underlying vector spaces $$0\\longrightarrow M'\\xrightarrow{\\iota}M\\xrightarrow{q}M''\n \\longrightarrow0$$ whose maps and actions respect complete steps. The action on $N$ is continuous. These $N$ form a filtered system whose union is $M$, and $$C^\\bullet_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)\n           =\\mathop{\\mathrm{colim}}_N C^\\bullet_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,N).$$*\n\n2.  *The ring $k[[G]]$ is Noetherian, and the trivial compact module $k$ has a resolution $P_\\bullet$ by finitely generated free compact $k[[G]]$-modules. Every term on the left is a finite power of $M$.*\n\n3.  *A right resolution by finitely generated free compact modules similarly defines $H_i(G,M)$.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-cts-local-section",
        "exact_quote": "Let $K$ be a normal uniform open subgroup of $G$, and let $X$ be a profinite $G$-space on which $K$ acts freely. Suppose that $X\\to Y=K\\backslash X$ has a continuous $K$-equivariant trivialization as a principal $K$-space. Put $H=G/K$. If $x\\in X$ and $y$ is its image, the finite group $G_x$ maps isomorphically to $H_y$. There is an $H_y$-invariant clopen neighborhood $V$ of $y$ and a section $s:V\\to X$, with $s(y)=x$, which is equivariant for $G_x\\simeq H_y$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-mark-whole-model",
        "exact_quote": "For each such $U$ there are a finite free $A_m$-algebra $A'$, with integral multiplication laws in a fixed basis, and a $G$-invariant idempotent $e\\in B'=A'[1/x]$ such that $$B_U=eB',\\qquad B'/B_m\\text{ is finite \\'{e}tale}.$$ As a semilinear $A_m$-module, $A'$ has a finite filtration whose quotients are basic coefficients in $\\mathscr C_m$.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-mark-roots",
        "exact_quote": "At level $\\ell$, the reduced closure over $A_m$ of lifted geometric étale bases has coordinate algebra $$R_{m,\\ell}=k[[t_{1,\\ell},\\ldots,t_{r,\\ell}]].$$ If $s_i=t_{i,\\ell}^{p^{m\\ell}}$, the intermediate algebra generated by the $s_i$ over $A_m$ is $$S_{m,\\ell}=k[[s_1,\\ldots,s_r]],\\qquad\n A_m\\subseteq S_{m,\\ell}.$$ After inverting $x$, $S_{m,\\ell}[1/x]$ is the étale basis algebra, and $R_{m,\\ell}[1/x]$ is its full generator-lift algebra. In particular the latter is the root extension of order $p^{m\\ell}$, finite free of rank $p^{m\\ell r}$, with no reduction of the lift scheme omitted. These identifications are natural under the $G$ action, changes of markings, and finite étale base change. For $j\\leq\\ell$, earlier division coordinates are integral series in the $p^{m(\\ell-j)}$ powers of the level-$\\ell$ coordinates.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-mark-finite-isotropy",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $U$ is a torsion-free product marking subgroup as above. Every finite subgroup $F\\subset G$ acts geometrically freely on $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Spec}}B_U$. There is an element $a_F\\in B_U$ with $$\\sum_{f\\in F}f(a_F)=1.$$ Multiplication by $a_F$ is continuous between bounded-denominator steps of finite coefficient bundles. It also acts continuously on bounded analytic section and compact-support models, with compact profinite parameters retained. Thus the geometric coefficient modules satisfy the trace and module-action hypotheses of [prop:cts-isotropy-bound,prop:cts-full-duality]. Equivalently they satisfy <a href=\"#def:cts-trace\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:cts-trace\">5</a>.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-kum-banach-limits",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(E_j,f_j)$ be a countable inverse system of complete nonarchimedean normed vector spaces, with continuous linear maps $f_j:E_{j+1}\\to E_j$ having dense image. Then $R^1\\!\\varprojlim_j E_j=0$. The assertion holds after replacing $E_j$ by $C(\\mathcal D,E_j)$ with its supremum norm for any compact profinite $\\mathcal D$. Consequently a countable inverse system of complexes having this property in each degree is computed by its termwise inverse limit.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-kum-annulus",
        "exact_quote": "The Kummer tower on $A_S[a,b]$ gives a natural complex $$\\label{eq:kum-difference}\n \\mathbf R\\Gamma(A_S[a,b],\\mathcal O^\\flat)\n \\simeq\n \\left[M_R[a,b]\\xrightarrow{\\gamma-1}M_R[a,b]\\right],\n \\qquad \\gamma(T^u)=\\epsilon^uT^u,$$ in degrees $0,1$. If $$\\label{eq:kum-gap}\n a<a'<b'<b,\\qquad\n a'/a\\geq e^\\kappa,\\qquad b/b'\\geq e^\\kappa,$$ restriction to $A_S[a',b']$ is chain homotopic to its constant-monomial part. It therefore factors through $R[0]\\oplus R[-1]$ in the derived category. The homotopy is bounded, linear over $R$, uniform for every compact profinite parameter, and compatible with base change and a translation of the coordinate by a relative section.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-kum-line",
        "exact_quote": "The following statements hold over $S$, naturally under base change, with arbitrary retained compact profinite parameters.*\n\n1.  *There is a constant $A_p>1$, depending only on $p$ and the chosen Kummer generator, such that for $r_{\\mathrm{out}}/r\\geq A_p$ the map $$\\mathbf R\\Gamma(D_S(c,r_{\\mathrm{out}}),\\mathcal O^\\flat)\n     \\longrightarrow\\mathbf R\\Gamma(D_S(c,r),\\mathcal O^\\flat)$$ factors through evaluation $R[0]$ followed by the constant inclusion. In particular, $$H^0(D_S(c,r),\\mathcal O^\\flat)=R,$$ and $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{colim}}_{r\\to0}\\mathbf R\\Gamma(D_S(c,r),\\mathcal O^\\flat)\\simeq R[0].$$*\n\n\n2.  *Ordinary and compactly supported cohomology of the line are $$\\label{eq:kum-line-values}\n     \\mathbf R\\Gamma(\\mathbb A_S,\\mathcal O^\\flat)\\simeq R[0],\n     \\qquad\n     \\mathbf R\\Gamma_c(\\mathbb A_S,\\mathcal O^\\flat)\\simeq R[-2].$$ For two concentric support discs with a sufficiently large radius ratio, the map from the smaller support complex to the larger one has pure degree-two image, carried isomorphically into the final compact-support cohomology. More precisely, if $A_r$ is the support complex for the disc of radius $r$ and $q_r:A_r\\to R[-2]$ is extension of support to the whole line, the cone of $q_r$ maps cohomologically to zero after that fixed enlargement. The required ratio is uniform, also under bounded translations of the centers.*\n\n3.  *For $d$ ordered affine coordinates, the ordinary and section-germ complexes are $R[0]$, and the compact-support complex computed by cofinal boxes is $R[-2d]$. Maps between box-support bounds have pure degree-$2d$ image after a fixed enlargement in each coordinate.*\n\n4.  *The analogous relative assertions with $\\mathbb F_p$ coefficients hold with the base complex $\\mathbf R\\Gamma(S,\\mathbb F_p)$ in place of $R$. For $S=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Spa}}(C^\\flat,\\mathcal O_{C^\\flat})\\times\\mathcal D$ this base complex is $C(\\mathcal D,\\mathbb F_p)[0]$. With the chosen geometric orientations, extension of constants identifies these line, section-germ, and support computations with the corresponding $R_{\\mathcal D}$ computations above.*\n\n*The degree-two support class is unchanged by a translation of its section. Under inclusion of finitely many disjoint support discs into one larger disc, their degree-two classes add.",
        "source_id": "PM-313.1"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-kum-low-support",
        "exact_quote": "Let $X$ be a bounded relative chart in an untilted affine space over a base v-sheaf $B$, with a slightly larger chart available for collars, and let $Z\\subset X$ be closed. Assume the following conditions on this fixed bound.*\n\n1.  *After a finite cover of a slightly enlarged base bound by qc charts, $Z$ has a cofinal decreasing sequence of neighborhoods $T_j$, each a finite disjoint union of relative discs, or of boxes in at least one normal affine coordinate. Their centers are actual analytic sections on those charts.*\n\n2.  *On each chart, the clusters of $T_{j+1}$ refine those of $T_j$, and a fixed further refinement $j\\mapsto j+N$ puts every child cluster in its parent with the radius ratio required in <a href=\"#prop:kum-line\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:kum-line\">25</a>. The same $N$ works for every $j$, for all compact parameters, and on the finitely many support shells used for excision.*\n\n3.  *The cluster bounds have separated outer collars inside the enlarged output chart. Their intersection is $Z$, and their complements admissibly exhaust $X\\setminus Z$.*\n\n*For $\\mathscr F=\\mathcal O^\\flat$ or $\\mathbb F_p$, put $$E_j=\\operatorname{fib}\\bigl(\\mathbf R\\Gamma(X,\\mathscr F)\n              \\longrightarrow\\mathbf R\\Gamma(X\\setminus T_j,\\mathscr F)\n                       \\bigr).$$ The inverse systems $H^0(E_j)$ and $H^1(E_j)$ are pro-zero. The same assertion holds relatively on the base and with compact parameters. Consequently the complex with support in $Z$ has no cohomology in degrees zero or one, and deletion of $Z$ preserves relative degree-zero sections. These conclusions hold also after a bounded-below descent calculation for which the finite chart refinements above can be made in each fixed total degree.*\n\n*For a closed locus $Z\\subset Y$ in a possibly unbounded relative untilted affine space, the same low-degree support vanishing and degree-zero deletion statement hold if $Y$ has a compatible countable admissible exhaustion by interleaved bounds $X_a$ on which these hypotheses hold for $Z\\cap X_a$. The tube systems and their required refinements may depend on $a$.",
        "source_id": "PM-313.1"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-ind-lattice-transitions",
        "exact_quote": "Let $L$ be a lattice of rank $e$ in a finite-dimensional $\\mathbb Q_p$-vector space, and let $L'=p^{-1}L$. With trivial characteristic-$p$ coefficients, continuous cohomology is the exterior algebra on $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}_{\\mathrm{cts}}(L,\\mathbb F_p)$. Under the identifications from a lattice basis,*\n\n1.  *restriction from $L'$ to $L$ is zero in positive degrees and is the identity in degree zero;*\n\n2.  *corestriction from $L$ to $L'$ is zero in degrees less than $e$ and identifies the top-degree orientation lines.*\n\n*The assertions hold with coefficients $R_{\\mathcal D}$ and with relative base complexes in place of $\\mathbb F_p$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-ind-tubes",
        "exact_quote": "Let a quasicompact perfectoid chart over $C^\\flat$ carry untilted coordinates $z_1,\\ldots,z_t$ whose classes in $\\mathcal N_m$ are independent. Restrict to a bounded part of this chart and to a compact open slope patch in $\\mathbb Q_p^t$. After a finite refinement of the base by quasicompact charts, the following constructions are available on each member of the refinement.*\n\n\n1.  *There are radii $0<\\alpha<\\beta$ and a fixed lattice $L\\subset \\mathbb Q_p^t\\oplus F_m$ such that, on every geometric fiber, $$\\label{eq:ind-persistent-lattice}\n           L=\\{w:|\\ell_z(w)|\\leq\\alpha\\}\n            =\\{w:|\\ell_z(w)|<\\beta\\},\n           \\qquad\n           \\ell_z(a,b)=\\sum_i a_i z_i+b.$$ The same base chart has lattice $p^jL$ for the radii $\\alpha|p|^j$ and $\\beta|p|^j$, for every integer $j$.*\n\n2.  *Write $L_a=\\operatorname{pr}_{\\mathbb Q_p^t}(L)$ and $L_b=L\\cap F_m$. At every sufficiently large $j$, the slope patch is a finite union of $p^jL_a$-cosets. Its graph in $\\mathcal N_m$ has disjoint tubular neighborhoods indexed by those cosets. Each tube is the image of an actual relative disc, centered at a section $\\sum_i a_i z_i$ for a constant representative $a$, modulo the compact translation lattice $p^jL_b$.*\n\n3.  *The closed tubes of radius $\\alpha|p|^j$ and the open tubes of radius $\\beta|p|^j$ are interleaved and cofinal among neighborhoods of the graph family. The construction works on a slightly enlarged independent-base bound and on its support collars, and it retains an arbitrary compact profinite parameter $\\mathcal D$.*\n\n*For finitely many added coordinates and compact open patches of matrices of slopes, take products of these constructions. Their finite base refinements can be chosen simultaneously.",
        "source_id": "PM-313.1"
      },

        "exact_quote": "For every $s\\geq0$ and every compact profinite $\\mathcal D$, extension of constants induces natural quasi-isomorphisms $$\\begin{aligned}\n E_{\\mathcal D}\\otimes_{\\mathbb F_p}\\mathbf R\\Gamma_c(Y_s,\\mathbb F_p)\n   &\\xrightarrow{\\ \\sim\\ }\n       \\mathbf R\\Gamma_c(Y_s\\times\\underline{\\mathcal D},\\mathbb F_p),\n       \\label{eq:ind-fp-parameters}\\\\\n R_{\\mathcal D}\\otimes_{\\mathbb F_p}\\mathbf R\\Gamma_c(Y_s,\\mathbb F_p)\n   &\\xrightarrow{\\ \\sim\\ }\n       \\mathbf R\\Gamma_c(Y_s\\times\\underline{\\mathcal D},\\mathcal O^\\flat).\n       \\label{eq:ind-algebraic-comparison}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The tensors are algebraic.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-ind-admissible-cohomology",
        "exact_quote": "Let $H$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group and let $V$ be a countable smooth admissible $\\mathbb F_p[H]$-module. Then $H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(H,V)$ is finite-dimensional for every $a$. Let $H$ act trivially on the external parameter $\\mathcal D$ and on $R_{\\mathcal D}$, and diagonally through $V$ on $R_{\\mathcal D}\\otimes V$. For the coefficient topology supplied by uniform finite-span families, there is a natural isomorphism $$H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(H,R_{\\mathcal D}\\otimes_{\\mathbb F_p}V)\n \\cong R_{\\mathcal D}\\otimes_{\\mathbb F_p}H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(H,V).$$",
        "source_id": "PM-313.1"
      },

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-laurent-action",
        "exact_quote": "The $G$-action on $W$ and on $\\mathscr W_{\\mathcal D}$ is jointly continuous from a complete step, with a compact set of group and parameter values, into a complete step. It is uniformly equicontinuous there. The same holds for multiplication by the finite marked function algebra, fixed root-basis changes, and the finite matrices occurring in continuous group resolutions. Absolute Frobenius is an invertible additive operator on these modules. Its sufficiently divisible powers fixing $k$ commute with $G$ and act by chain automorphisms on the group complexes over $k$.",
        "source_id": "PM-313.1"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-laurent-action",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Coefficient module with complete steps** ([source](#stmt-def-cts-steps)): A coefficient module with complete steps is a vector space $M=\bigcup_{a\geq 0}M_a$, where the $M_a$ are complete Hausdorff linearly topologized $k$-spaces and the inclusions are continuous injections.
- **Bounded-step continuous cochains** ([source](#stmt-def-cts-steps)): We use the bounded-step continuous cochains $$C^j_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)=\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_a C_{\mathrm{cts}}(G^j,M_a)$$ with the usual inhomogeneous differential.
- **Trace-admissible semilinear module** ([source](#stmt-def-cts-trace)): A semilinear $A$-module $M$ with complete steps is trace-admissible if, for every finite subgroup $F\subset G$, there is $t_F\in A$ satisfying $$\sum_{f\in F}f(t_F)=1,$$ and multiplication by $t_F$ carries each complete step continuously into some complete step.
- **Semilinear action** ([source](#stmt-def-cts-trace)): The action is semilinear in the sense that $g(am)=g(a)g(m)$.
- **Powered division algebra** ([source](#pm-h-11)): For $\ell\geq1$ and $0\leq b\leq m\ell$, define $$D_m(\ell,b) =A_m[\,T^{p^b}\,]\ \subseteq\ A_m[[T]]/([p^\ell]_{\mathcal F}(T)).$$
- **Basic coefficients** ([source](#stmt-def-mark-coefficients)): The basic coefficients at height $m$ are $$\mathcal L_m^{\otimes w}\otimes_{A_m} \bigotimes_{j=1}^{s}D_m(\ell_j,b_j), \qquad w\in\mathbb Z,\quad 0\leq b_j\leq m\ell_j, \label{eq:mark-basic-coefficients}$$ where $s$ may be zero.
- **Allowed coefficient class** ([source](#stmt-def-mark-coefficients)): The allowed class $\mathscr C_m$ is their closure under finite direct sums, tensor products, equivariant direct summands, and finite equivariant filtrations whose successive quotients belong to the class.
- **Compact support as restriction fibers** ([source](#eq:ind-support-convention)): All cohomology is on the $v$-site. We use the support convention of <a href="#sec:kummer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:kummer">1</a>: for an increasing, interleaved system of quasicompact bounds $K\Subset X$, $$\label{eq:ind-support-convention} \mathbf R\Gamma_c(X,\mathscr E) =\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_K\operatorname{fib} \bigl(\mathbf R\Gamma(X,\mathscr E) \longrightarrow\mathbf R\Gamma(X\setminus K,\mathscr E)\bigr).$$
- **Root module by transport and restriction of scalars** ([source](#pm-h-36)): If $h$ is a power of $p$ fixing $k$ and $M$ is an $R$-module, $M^{1/h}$ is the copy of $M$ transported along the isomorphism $$R\longrightarrow R^{1/h},\qquad b\longmapsto b^{1/h}.$$
- **Translation augmentation** ([source](#pm-h-37)): For a finite translation quotient $H$, a *translation augmentation* means a nonzero $H$-equivariant map $\lambda:\mathcal O(H)\to k$, with trivial action on $k$.
- **Coefficient-only Frobenius** ([source](#pm-h-41)): The operator $\varphi$ used in this subsection raises coefficients in $F$ to their $Q_k$th powers and fixes $x^I$, $y^{-J}$, and every $b_\nu$.
- **Positive Laurent subspace** ([source](#stmt-auto-definition-1)): An element $w\in W$ belongs to $W_+$ if, in some normalized basis $b_{i,h}$, every nonzero coefficient monomial of $w$ has $I\geq\epsilon$ for some real $\epsilon>0$.
- **Derived completeness convention** ([source](#pm-h-62)): We use derived $p$-completeness in the form $$X\simeq\operatorname*{holim}_a X/p^a.$$

| id | quantity | relation | value | regime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| q-powered-division-rank | Rank of the powered division algebra over its height-stratum base | = | $p^{n\ell-b}$ | The permitted division level and powered-coordinate index. |
| q-connected-jet-rank | Rank of the integral connected marking model | = | $(p^m-1)p^{mh}$ | A fixed exact-height open and finite connected jet order. |
| q-generator-lift-rank | Rank of the full generator-lift root extension | = | $p^{m\ell r}$ | A finite division level on the chosen height stratum. |
| q-uniform-isotropy-degree-threshold | Degree above which the uniform finite-isotropy vanishing holds | = | $a_Gd_G$ | The subgroup and bound are independent of the coefficient and its finite twist. |
| q-ordinary-stabilizer-dimension | Dimension of the ordinary Morava stabilizer | = | $n^2$ | The chosen positive height. |
| q-annular-narrowing-ratio | Required lower bound on each annular radial ratio | = | $e^\kappa$ | The fixed Kummer generator determines the denominator constant; compact parameters retain the same bound. |
| q-translation-distribution-dimension | Dimension of the translation distribution power-series ring | = | $(m-1)r$ | The higher intermediate-height case. |
| q-coinduced-coordinate-dimension | Dimension of the finite translation coordinate representation | = | $q^d=h^r=p^{m\ell r}$ | Allowed powers fixing the finite constant field. |
| q-stable-lattice-threshold | Chosen compact-lattice pole allowance | > | $\frac{c_S+1}{1-h_0^{-1}}$ | The fixed transfer and finite marking stage; the pole constant is not numerically specified. |
| q-positive-frobenius-contraction | Norm of the positive Laurent tuple after the initial basis adjustment and further powering | ≤ | $\exp(-\alpha h_0^a)$ | The step and positive constants may depend on the finite tuple. |
| q-height-one-adams-valuation | Valuation of the nonzero Adams-operation multiplier | = | $1+\nu_p(t)$ | Nonzero integer exponents satisfying the retained periodicity condition. |
