<a id="eq:sphere-cofiber-short"></a>
*Proof.* The cofiber exact sequence gives, for every $j$, $$\label{eq:sphere-cofiber-short}
 0\longrightarrow \pi_jX/p\pi_jX
 \longrightarrow \pi_j(X/p)
 \longrightarrow (\pi_{j-1}X)[p]
 \longrightarrow0.$$ Both end terms are killed by $p$. Thus every finite middle term is a finite $p$-group; we do not require it to be killed by $p$ itself. Factoring $p^{a+1}$ as $p\circ p^a$ gives exact triangles $$X/p^a\longrightarrow X/p^{a+1}\longrightarrow X/p.$$ Their homotopy exact sequences inductively show that $\pi_j(X/p^a)$ is a finite $p$-group for every $a\geq1$ and every $j$.

<a id="eq:sphere-finite-limit"></a>
For fixed $j$, the inverse system of these finite groups is Mittag–Leffler: its decreasing images in any one finite target eventually stabilize. Its first derived inverse limit therefore vanishes. Applying the Milnor exact sequence, in the adjacent degree as well, and derived completeness gives $$\label{eq:sphere-finite-limit}
 \pi_jX\ \cong\ \varprojlim_a\pi_j(X/p^a).$$ For clarity, vanishing of the derived limit requires no surjectivity of the transition maps. The map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product of the finite groups is surjective: every finite set of its defining equations can be solved backwards, and compactness of the product supplies a simultaneous solution. This is also a direct proof of the required lim-one vanishing.

Put $M=\pi_jX$. The presentation <a href="#eq:sphere-finite-limit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:sphere-finite-limit">[eq:sphere-finite-limit]</a> makes $M$ a compact Hausdorff pro-$p$ group with its canonical continuous $\mathbb Z_p$-module structure. On each finite target $\pi_j(X/p^a)$, this scalar structure is defined by reducing a $p$-adic integer modulo a power of $p$ that kills that target; the definitions are compatible with the transition maps. Multiplication by $p$ on $M$ is continuous, so $pM$ is compact and closed. By <a href="#eq:sphere-cofiber-short" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:sphere-cofiber-short">[eq:sphere-cofiber-short]</a>, the quotient $M/pM$ is finite.

Choose $a_1,\ldots,a_d\in M$ lifting generators of $M/pM$ over $\mathbb F_p$. For $z\in M$, successively express $$z_\ell=\sum_{i=1}^d b_{i,\ell}a_i+pz_{\ell+1},
 \qquad z_0=z,\qquad b_{i,\ell}\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}.$$ The scalars $c_i=\sum_{\ell\geq0}p^\ell b_{i,\ell}$ converge in $\mathbb Z_p$. The residual term after $L$ steps is $p^Lz_L$. It tends to zero in $M$: any fixed finite target in <a href="#eq:sphere-finite-limit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:sphere-finite-limit">[eq:sphere-finite-limit]</a> is killed by a fixed power of $p$, which kills the image of $p^Lz_L$ for all sufficiently large $L$, independently of $z_L$. Therefore $z=\sum_i c_i a_i$. The continuous homomorphism $$\mathbb Z_p^d\longrightarrow M,\qquad (c_i)\longmapsto\sum_i c_i a_i$$ is surjective. This proves finite generation as an abstract $\mathbb Z_p$-module, and not merely density of a finitely generated subgroup.

Conversely, if every $\pi_jX$ is finitely generated over $\mathbb Z_p$, then both end terms of <a href="#eq:sphere-cofiber-short" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:sphere-cofiber-short">[eq:sphere-cofiber-short]</a> are finite. For the $p$-torsion term, use that a submodule of a finite module over the Noetherian ring $\mathbb Z_p$ is finite as a module, and here it is killed by $p$. The middle term is consequently finite as well. ◻

</details>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-sphere-completion-2"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-sphere-completion</summary>

*Proof of [thm:main](#thm:main).* Let $X=L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$. A $K(n)$-local spectrum is derived $p$-complete when $n>0$. To see this directly, the fiber of $X\to\operatorname*{holim}_aX/p^a$ is $$\operatorname*{holim}(\cdots\xrightarrow{p}X\xrightarrow{p}X)
 \simeq F(S[1/p],X).$$ The spectrum $S[1/p]$ is $K(n)$-acyclic, so this mapping spectrum vanishes by locality. This proves the required completeness without a connectivity assumption.

The map $S\to S_p^\wedge$ is a mod-$p$ equivalence, hence a $K(n)$-equivalence: its cofiber has invertible multiplication by $p$, whereas multiplication by $p$ is zero on Morava $K$-theory. Exactness of localization therefore identifies $$X\simeq L_{K(n)}S,\qquad X/p\simeq L_{K(n)}(S/p).$$ The latter spectrum has finite homotopy groups in every degree by . Applying proves the sphere assertion.

For the finite-spectrum formulation, consider the class of finite $p$-local spectra $F$ for which every $\pi_j L_{K(n)}(F\wedge S/p)$ is finite. It contains the sphere by and is closed under suspensions, finite cofiber sequences, and retracts, by exactness and the homotopy long exact sequence. It therefore contains every finite $p$-local spectrum. The spectrum $L_{K(n)}F$ is derived $p$-complete by the same locality argument, and its cofiber of $p$ is $L_{K(n)}(F\wedge S/p)$. Applying objectwise proves the full finite-spectrum conclusion of [thm:main](#thm:main). ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-63"></a>
###### Ranks and the height-one calculation

Finite generation gives an abstract decomposition $$\pi_jL_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge
 \cong\mathbb Z_p^{\,r_{p,n,j}}
   \oplus\bigoplus_{e\geq1}
          (\mathbb Z/p^e)^{m_{p,n,j,e}},$$ with finitely many nonzero torsion multiplicities in each degree. The argument above establishes the existence of these finite invariants; it does not determine the torsion multiplicities in general.

<a id="stmt-cor-sphere-ranks"></a>
<div id="cor:sphere-ranks" class="corollary">

<a id="eq:sphere-ranks"></a>
**Corollary 66**. *For every prime $p$, every $n\geq1$, and every $j\in\mathbb Z$, the free rank is $$\label{eq:sphere-ranks}
 r_{p,n,j}
   =\#\left\{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}:
            \sum_{i\in I}(1-2i)=j\right\}.$$ Equivalently, these ranks are the graded dimensions of the exterior $\mathbb Q_p$-algebra on generators in degrees $-1,-3,\ldots,-(2n-1)$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cor-sphere-ranks"><summary>Proof of stmt-cor-sphere-ranks</summary>

*Proof.* By Barthel et al. (2025, Theorem A) <a id="pm-cite-80"></a>[[bssw2024](#ref-bssw2024)], the rationalized homotopy ring is the indicated exterior algebra. For a finitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module its $\mathbb Q_p$-dimension after inverting $p$ is its free rank. The exterior monomials are indexed by subsets $I$ and have the degrees in <a href="#eq:sphere-ranks" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:sphere-ranks">[eq:sphere-ranks]</a>. This proves the formula. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-prop-sphere-height-one"></a>
<div id="prop:sphere-height-one" class="proposition">

**Proposition 67**. *Let $p$ be odd. Then, for every $j\in\mathbb Z$, $$\pi_jL_{K(1)}S_p^\wedge\cong
 \begin{cases}
  \mathbb Z_p, & j=0\text{ or }j=-1,\\
  \mathbb Z/p^{\,1+\nu_p(t)},
       & j=2t-1,\quad0\neq t\in(p-1)\mathbb Z,\\
  0, & \text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}$$ The displayed groups include all additive extensions.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-sphere-height-one"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-sphere-height-one</summary>

<a id="eq:sphere-height-one-valuation"></a>
*Proof.* At height one, Morava $E$-theory is $p$-completed periodic complex $K$-theory, with $$\pi_*KU_p^\wedge=\mathbb Z_p[\beta^{\pm1}],\qquad |\beta|=2.$$ The stabilizer is $\mathbb Z_p^\times=\mu_{p-1}\times(1+p\mathbb Z_p)$, and the Adams operation $\psi^a$ acts on $\beta^t$ by $a^t$. Taking homotopy fixed points by the finite group $\mu_{p-1}$ is exact on these coefficient modules, because $p-1$ is a unit in $\mathbb Z_p$. The resulting Adams summand, denoted $B$, has $$\pi_{2t}B=
 \begin{cases}\mathbb Z_p,&(p-1)\mid t,\\0,&(p-1)\nmid t,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad \pi_{2t+1}B=0.$$ The element $1+p$ topologically generates $1+p\mathbb Z_p$. Its two-term continuous resolution, or the standard Adams-operation fiber sequence (Hopkins 2014, secs. 1–2) <a id="pm-cite-81"></a>[[hopkinsKOne](#ref-hopkinsKOne)], gives $$L_{K(1)}S_p^\wedge\longrightarrow B
 \xrightarrow{\,\psi^{1+p}-1\,}B.$$ On a retained coefficient in degree $2t$, the map is multiplication by $(1+p)^t-1$. For $t=0$ it is zero, giving $\mathbb Z_p$ in degrees $0$ and $-1$. For $t\neq0$ it is injective, and its cokernel is cyclic of order determined by $$\label{eq:sphere-height-one-valuation}
 \nu_p\bigl((1+p)^t-1\bigr)=1+\nu_p(t).$$ Indeed, if $p\nmid a$, binomial expansion gives $(1+p)^a-1\equiv ap\pmod{p^2}$. If $v_p(z)\geq1$ and $p$ is odd, the term $pz$ in $(1+z)^p-1$ has valuation $1+v_p(z)$ and every other term has strictly greater valuation. Iterating this observation proves <a href="#eq:sphere-height-one-valuation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:sphere-height-one-valuation">[eq:sphere-height-one-valuation]</a> for positive $t$. For negative $t$, the identity $$(1+p)^{-t}-1=-\frac{(1+p)^t-1}{(1+p)^t}$$ shows that the valuation is unchanged by replacing $t$ with $-t$.

The cokernel for a nonzero retained $t$ lies in degree $2t-1$; there is no kernel in degree $2t$. Coefficients in other degrees vanish. The fiber exact sequence has at most one contributing kernel or cokernel in each stem, so the stated groups involve no unresolved additive extension. ◻

</details>

      "explanation": "Degreewise finite generation and explicit rational ranks of the local sphere provide foundational invariants necessary for constructing and filtering chromatic overlap spectra.",
      "relation": "prerequisite",
      "source_anchor": "thm:descent-integral",
      "source_pm_id": "PM-313.1",
      "source_quote": "the $\\mathbb Z_p$-module $$\\pi_t L_{K(n)}S_p^\\wedge$$ is finitely generated.",
      "target_anchor": "stmt-thm-main",
      "target_pm_id": "PM-318.1",
      "target_quote": "Then $X=L_{n-1}D$ has the filtration and unit compatibility",
      "verification": "PENDING"
    },
    {
      "basis": "inferred",
      "direction": "symmetric",
      "explanation": "Both works analyze actions and invariant structures under open subgroups of the stabilizer group.",
      "relation": "shared_technique",
      "source_anchor": "stmt-lem-cts-comparison",
      "source_pm_id": "PM-313.1",
      "source_quote": "There is an $H_y$-invariant clopen neighborhood $V$ of $y$ and a section $s:V\\to X$, with $s(y)=x$, which is equivariant for $G_x\\simeq H_y$.",
      "target_anchor": "thm:invariant-radicals",
      "target_pm_id": "PM-311.1",
      "target_quote": "Let $U\\subseteq A_n^\\times$ be any open subgroup.",
      "verification": "PENDING"
    },

      "basis": "inferred",
      "direction": "directed",
      "explanation": "The determination of the rational homotopy ranks as exterior algebra dimensions over generators of odd degrees fixes the stage count and shift degrees appearing in the height three cofibers.",
      "relation": "prerequisite",
      "source_anchor": "cor:sphere-ranks",
      "source_pm_id": "PM-313.1",
      "source_quote": "Equivalently, these ranks are the graded dimensions of the exterior",

      "target_pm_id": "PM-318.2",
      "target_quote": "whose successive cofibers $C_i=\\mathop{\\mathrm{cofib}}(F_{i-1}\\to F_i)$",
      "verification": "PENDING"
    }
